mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 3.5% (as of the signal date).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over the past 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE has risen by more than 0.3pp in the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: The joint behavior of inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) drives equity returns: when CPIAUCSL is above 3.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS is not declining, the market perceives inflationary pressure without accommodative policy, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS change in 3 months <= 0.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing slowdown regime (INDPRO declining for 3 consecutive months), reduced corporate output and earnings growth drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when INDPRO has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand for durable goods and housing, which boosts corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the trading days where HOUST has increased by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation, which triggers the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) signals a deteriorating consumer sector, which reduces corporate sales growth and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS has decreased by more than 0.5% in the prior 3 months and RSAFS has increased by more than 1% in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of labor market deterioration (UNRATE > 4.5%) and high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), reduced consumer spending and corporate profit margins drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: labor market deterioration with high interest rates
failure_condition: The S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.
